pairs.why: Rendering is nearly identical, but A adds vent slits on the side shell, so it reads slightly more like a built helmet, which the saddle lessons rewarded.
Same pair with the sides swapped: B has the side vent detail and A's shell is plain, so B is slightly more convincingly built.
A adds a side panel and collar tabs that give the helmet believable construction like the real vending machine and phone booth, while B is a bare smooth shell.
B carries the side panel and collar clasps, so it is more built like a real object; A's plain shell leans toward a statue.
B's gold pins wrap over the board edge as real 3D leads, while A's pads are flat and painted on, so B reads more like a real toy-scale object.
A's pins bend down over the edge like real chip leads, while B's are flat surface pads that look like a sticker.
B's raised gold pin blocks add dimension and a toy-like build closer to the chunky real cards, while A's flat painted pads read as printed.
A's raised pin blocks give a more tangible, built-object read than B's flat pads, even though shading and finish are otherwise matched.
